exposure: Bilateral ligation of the descending uterine artery branches
two autonomous balloon Zhukovsky catheters (vaginal and uterine)
Group 2: Group 1 interventions + balloon tamponade using an intrauterine Zhukovsky catheter
excision of a small area of placenta accreta
Group 3: Group 2 interventions + intravaginal Zhukovsky balloon catheter
Excision of a small area of placenta accreta or full metroplasty
bilateral ligation of the descending uterine artery branches
Group 1: Bilateral ligation, Barinov external supraplacental pleated sutures, and either excision of the tightly attached portion of placenta accreta or metroplasty
cohort: 92 pregnant women with placenta accreta undergoing a caesarean section
finding: The simultaneous use of intrauterine and intravaginal Zhukovsky balloon catheters during caesarean section reduced blood loss, blood transfusion rates, and the risk of hysterectomy in patients with placenta accreta.
mod_finding: The use of an intrauterine balloon catheter during cesarean section was associated with a reduction in blood loss and blood transfusions in women with placenta accreta.
